Eat the whole city for pocket change
intro: Korat's Michelin list is all Bib Gourmand, which is the best kind of problem: real quality, gentle prices. Start with Kai Yang Saeng Thai, the grilled chicken locals have championed for generations, and Pa Pleung Mhee Kratok, home of the noodle dish named after this region. Laab Somphit rounds it out at around 40 baht a plate.
quickAnswerHtml: Nakhon Ratchasima has 8 Michelin 2026 restaurants, all Bib Gourmand, with no starred spots yet.

Laab Somphit rounds it out at around 40 baht a plate.

blocks.name: Banmai Chay Nam
blocks.descHtml:
Banmai Chay Nam sits on Mittraphap Road right in the middle of Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima — easy to find since it's on the main road everyone already drives along to Khao Yai. There's parking on-site, and it's open roughly 09:00–21:00 daily (per local media reports; worth checking the restaurant's Facebook page before you go to be sure). Prices sit at the ฿฿ level by MICHELIN's rating, with mid-range Thai dishes meant for sharing — the per-head budget stays light, which makes it a good fit for families and larger groups. The restaurant accepts both Visa and Mastercard.

The restaurant is walk-in only — there's no online booking system. If you want to check ahead, you can call 081-660-2826. The times that need a bit of planning are weekends and the cool season, since that's Khao Yai's high season and the restaurant gets genuinely busy. The trick is to go before noon or wait until later in the afternoon, once the lunch rush has died down, for a more relaxed seat. If you're planning a Khao Yai trip, this restaurant works well either as your inbound meal before heading into the park, or as a send-off meal on the way back before getting on the motorway to Bangkok. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Minced beef curry in fresh-pressed coconut cream, with crispy fried snakeskin gourami — the dish MICHELIN highlighted in the 2026 guide
mustOrder: Minced beef curry in coconut cream with crispy fried snakeskin gourami
blocks.bestFor: A family/group meal on a Khao Yai road trip — mid-range riverside Thai food, in an old wooden house full of vintage collectibles
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Banmai Chay Nam Pak Chong official Facebook page

blocks.name: Kai Yang Saeng Thai
blocks.descHtml:
Kai Yang Saeng Thai is a takeaway-only shop with no seating, on Ratchadamnoen Road near Thao Suranari Monument (Ya Mo Monument), right in the middle of Korat's old town — an easy walk from Ya Mo Monument itself. A whole grilled chicken runs about 150-200 baht, depending on whether you choose the farmed breed or kai baan. Open daily from around 09:00-18:00 (some sources list 08:30-19:00). No advance booking needed since it's walk-in, but if you want to be sure, you can call ahead to reserve a chicken at 085-845-6604 or 044-241240. Cash only.

Good to know: the chicken here is grilled in rotisserie batches, and on some evenings it can sell out before closing time. If you're planning to buy after 3pm, calling ahead is a smart move so you don't miss out. The easiest time to go is late morning through early afternoon, when chicken is coming fresh off the grill all day. Anyone already visiting Ya Mo Monument or Wat Sala Loi can swing by easily since they're in the same area — buy your chicken, then find sticky rice and som tam nearby to turn it into a full meal on the spot, or carry it home as a Korat souvenir the way locals regularly do. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Charcoal rotisserie chicken marinated in a secret pepper-and-spice blend, served with sweet jaew dipping sauce
mustOrder: Rotisserie chicken marinated in secret pepper and herbs (whole)
blocks.bestFor: Lovers of good food at home-style prices, visitors dropping by Ya Mo Monument, anyone buying a Korat souvenir

blocks.name: Khanom Ochin
blocks.descHtml:
Khanom Ochin is a takeaway-only cart with no seating, on Chomsurangyat Road near the Nong Bua Rong intersection, in Korat's old town, not far from the Thao Suranari Monument, which doubles as a handy landmark for finding it. It's very easy on the wallet — under THB 100 a head — cash only, no advance booking. You'll need to queue in person (walk-in only). There's a phone number, 062-684-2484, for questions.

The cart starts selling around 3pm (MICHELIN lists 15:00-21:00), but in practice it sells out well before closing time, and usually earlier than the official hours suggest. The queue is legendary — people start lining up before 3pm — so the best time to go is right at opening, or a little before. Don't come in the evening; you'll likely find nothing left. One key thing to remember: the cart is closed on Wednesdays and Sundays, so plan your trip accordingly before driving out. The must-order is the salty Khanom Ochin — crispy fried dough wrapped around boldly seasoned glass noodles and vegetables — plus the homemade fried steamed buns. Grab extra to take home for family so you don't regret it later. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Salty Khanom Ochin — crispy fried dough wrapped around boldly seasoned glass-noodle-and-vegetable filling, a name only used in Korat and found nowhere else in Thailand
mustOrder: Salty Khanom Ochin (crispy fried dough with glass noodles and vegetables)
blocks.bestFor: Street food fans who want to bag a MICHELIN spot for under THB 100, and anyone passing through Korat looking for a one-of-a-kind souvenir snack

blocks.name: Krua Suwimol
blocks.bestFor: An easy-on-the-wallet all-night congee-style dinner with family or friends, and for drivers passing through on Mittraphap Road who want a MICHELIN-level bite without booking ahead
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Krua Suwimol Restaurant official Facebook page

blocks.name: Laab Somphit
blocks.descHtml:
Laab Somphit sits in Trok Chan, off Chan Road, in the middle of Old Korat, not far from the Thao Suranari Monument. Drive or take a songthaew into the old town and walk into the alley from there. The restaurant is open every day from around 07:00 until sometime in the afternoon to evening (sources differ on closing time, anywhere from 16:00 to 19:30 — if you're planning an evening visit, call ahead to check at 044-245-026). No reservations needed — just walk in and sit down.

Price is the main draw. Dishes start at around THB 40, and eating a proper meal runs about THB 100–250 per head, plenty to leave you full. MICHELIN lists the restaurant as cash only (Wongnai says it accepts credit cards), so to be safe, bring cash. The best time to go is late morning to around noon, since special dishes like mum and som neua are made in limited batches and aren't available every day — arrive earlier and you're more likely to find everything on offer. Dishes to make sure are on your table: laab or nam tok made to the Yasothon recipe, grilled beef tongue, grilled sweetbread, and grilled pork neck. Dress is casual, and it's an easy walk into the old town afterward. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Authentic Yasothon-recipe laab-koi-nam tok, with grilled beef tongue and grilled sweetbread
blocks.bestFor: Real Isan laab fans, an Old Korat walking food trail, and anyone looking for great food on a small budget, at Bib Gourmand level

blocks.name: Nub
blocks.descHtml:
Nub Phocana sits on Chomphon Road in Korat's old town, near the Wat Burapha night bazaar, an easy walk from the Thao Suranari Monument (Ya Mo). Prices are very light, around THB 60-80 a bowl. Open Monday to Saturday, roughly 08:30/09:30 to 15:00, closed Sundays. No booking needed — just walk in and take a seat. There's a shop phone number, 081-548-5481, if you want to check ahead, and importantly — cash only, so bring small bills.

The best time to go is late morning before noon, since the shop only sells during the morning-to-afternoon window and some of the stewed beef can run out before 3pm — go late and you might miss the best cuts. Getting around central Korat is easiest by car or a ride-hail drop-off on Chomphon Road; park along the old town streets and it's an easy walk from there. Fold it into a late-morning meal after paying respects to Ya Mo, or a stop before wandering the old town market — either way it fits right in. Order the mixed boiled beef plate to share, plus a bowl of clear beef noodle soup each, and you're looking at under 200 baht a head for a taste of Korat's newest Bib Gourmand. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Mixed boiled beef plate with dark soy sauce and lime, plus clear beef noodle soup simmered over charcoal
mustOrder: Mixed boiled beef plate (stewed beef, fresh beef, meatballs, offal, tossed with dark soy sauce and lime)
Clear beef noodle soup simmered over charcoal
blocks.bestFor: A late-morning to lunchtime beef noodle stop in Korat's old town, light on the wallet after paying respects to Ya Mo

blocks.name: Sow Jeck
blocks.descHtml:
Sow Jeck sits in the city centre of Korat, behind Maharat Nakhon Ratchasima Hospital, right at the entrance to Suranakhon Market on Maharat Road. Budget is easy on the wallet at around THB 100–250 per person, but it's cash only, so come prepared. The restaurant opens roughly 08:30–15:30 (some sources like Wongnai list it until 17:30, but it can close earlier once the food runs out), and no fixed closing day is listed, so it's worth calling ahead to check at 064-495-3655 — the same number you can use to book a table and order in advance.

It runs on a walk-in basis, but since making the Bib Gourmand list this small shop gets very busy, especially around lunchtime — walking straight in risks not getting a seat or a long wait. The most effective tip is to call ahead, book a table, and place your order before you set out, or go mid-morning before noon while the restaurant is still fairly quiet. The dishes to order are stir-fried seabass with celery, seafood pad kra pao, crab fried rice, and crispy pork stir-fried with salt and chilli. Getting there is easy — use Maharat Hospital as your landmark, then find the entrance to Suranakhon Market. Dress is casual. Read the full review →

mustOrder: Crispy pork stir-fried with salt and chilli
blocks.bestFor: Fans of made-to-order fresh seafood on a light budget who want a MICHELIN restaurant with real local-market atmosphere in Korat

faq.q: How many Michelin restaurants are in Nakhon Ratchasima?
faq.a: Eight in 2026, and every one is a Bib Gourmand. There are no starred restaurants here yet, so the whole list is about great food at honest prices.

faq.q: Which Korat dish should a first-timer try?
faq.a: Kai Yang Saeng Thai for grilled chicken and Pa Pleung Mhee Kratok for mee korat noodles are the two flavors tied to this city's name. With one meal to spare, start there.

faq.q: What is the cheapest Michelin spot in Korat?
faq.a: Laab Somphit, at roughly 40 baht a plate, is the lightest on the wallet. Nub follows close behind with noodles around 60 to 80 baht.

faq.q: Where can I sit down for a relaxed meal?
faq.a: Banmai Chay Nam serves riverside Thai food and Krua Suwimol does Thai-Chinese, both good for a long family lunch. Sow Jeck is a longtime local Thai kitchen worth a stop too.

faq.q: How do I get around to these restaurants?
faq.a: Most sit within Korat city, so a short drive or a local ride connects them quickly. Two or three stops in a day is very doable.
